summary: Tenanted pin attrition during canary population wave causing silent fallback to capacity-optimized variant
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled canary population wave for a tenant pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2, a subset of sessions silently lost their explicit pin and were served by the capacity-optimized variant (med-care-13b-q4_0) without an explicit fallback event in the control-plane logs. Impact: NimbusHealth reported inconsistent model outputs and a ~3x increase in tokens billed to the capacity-optimized variant for pinned routes, resulting in degraded prediction quality for a health assistant flow. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod us-west-1, tenant scoped routing with explicit model pin on route '/v1/assist'. Observed behavior: pins observed to expire rapidly during canary population wave (approx 2026-03-10 02:15-02:45 UTC) leading to silent reroute to capacity-optimized instance group. No explicit orchestrator rollback or canary weight change was requested by the customer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant creates explicit model pin to redwood-open-7b-v2 on route /v1/assist
2) Trigger canary population wave by scaling new canary instances in us-west-1 (orchestrator job id 2147)
3) Send a steady stream of pinned session requests (100 req/min) for 20 minutes
4) Observe routing decisions and final model served in ingest logs and billing records
logs: 2026-03-10T02:18:11Z edge-proxy INFO request 7fc3: tenant=nimbus route=/v1/assist pin=redwood-open-7b-v2 -> routedTo=med-care-13b-q4_0 (no explicit fallback flag)
2026-03-10T02:19:02Z orchestrator WARN pin-lease-check tenant=nimbus lease_remaining=1s shard=us-west-1
2026-03-10T02:19:03Z edge-proxy DEBUG affinity-lease-refresh tenant=nimbus result=timeout (rpc timeout=250ms)
metrics_snippets: p99_latency_edge_ms increases 120ms -> 360ms for pinned sessions during the wave
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - NimbusHealth: We started seeing wrong answers in clinical assistant results and a billing spike. Some requests show different model ids in logs.
2026-03-10 03:08 UTC - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged, opening incident and collecting logs. Asking for recent request IDs and sample inputs.
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - NimbusHealth: Provided sample request IDs and said issue persisted ~30 minutes. They are on a dedicated contract and require root-cause and mitigation steps.
comments: Aisha (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial triage - reproduces against dedicated pool, suspect lease renewal race during canary prewarm. Forwarded to SRE.

Diego (SRE) 2026-03-10: Observed orchestrator prewarm spike concurrent with lease renew window; edge rpc timeouts spiked to 12% during wave. Hypothesis: prewarm pressure increased RPC latency, causing expensive lease renews to fail and pins to expire.

Morgan (Serving Eng) 2026-03-11: Confirmed med-care variant was available in capacity-only shards; routing policy falls back to capacity-optimized variant when pin resolution fails. Need to validate pin-lease backoff and edge retry logic.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12: Notified NimbusHealth of temporary mitigation steps and planned follow-ups.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Lease renewal RPC timeouts from edge->orchestrator under increased prewarm load cause lease counters to drop and automatic pin expiry to occur.
Hypothesis 2: Orchestrator snapshot applied during population wave overwrote ephemeral pin metadata for active sessions due to a race between snapshot commit and lease refresh handlers.

Observed: No explicit canary weight change; control-plane audit logs show snapshot commit id 20260310-2147 at 02:19:03 UTC concurrent with prewarm jobs. Edge retries show increased latency and immediate 250ms RPC timeouts.
Reproduction in staging: Running scaled prewarm job reproduced pin attrition when edge RPC timeout set to 200-300ms; increasing edge rpc timeout to 800ms prevented attrition in tests.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): temporarily bumped edge->orchestrator rpc timeout to 800ms for us-west-1 dedicated pool and applied a pin-lease grace window (30s) on the serving-runtime to avoid immediate expiry on failed renew. NimbusHealth routed back to pinned variant and confirmed quality restored. These are emergency mitigations; permanent fix requires orchestrator commit ordering hardening and pin-lease renew backpressure handling.
action_items: ENG-ORCH-4321: Harden orchestrator snapshot commit ordering to ensure pin metadata merges don't clobber active lease state (owner: Morgan)
ENG-SERV-4312: Add exponential backoff and jitter to pin-lease renewal attempts and increase default grace window for dedicated pools (owner: Diego)
SRE-ROTATION-221: Add prewarm job rate limiter to avoid edge rpc saturation during population waves (owner: Priya)
Support: Follow up with NimbusHealth with postmortem and billing remediation proposal (owner: Aisha)
